title: Rahul Gandhi's 'economic disaster' remark at Columbia sets off BJP-Congress row
dek: The Leader of the Opposition told a New York audience India faces mass unemployment and a weak manufacturing base; the BJP called it 'anti-India propaganda', and the Congress said the government cares more about his words than the economy.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Remarks by Rahul Gandhi, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, at Columbia University in New York have set off a sharp exchange between the BJP and the Congress, with the ruling party accusing him of damaging India's image abroad and the Congress saying the government is more worried about criticism than about the economy.

Speaking at a fireside chat at the university on Tuesday, Gandhi said "India is sitting on an economic disaster", pointing to mass unemployment, a weak manufacturing base and problems in the education system, according to reports of the event. He also repeated his party's allegation of "vote chori" (vote theft), saying that "from the day your elections are rigged, the politics has stopped", and said the Congress was in "a pretty good position" in Uttar Pradesh, where his party has an alliance ahead of the 2027 Assembly election.

## What the BJP said

At a press conference at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi on Wednesday, party spokesperson Gaurav Bhatia said Gandhi had made "false statements" and "baseless allegations", accused him of a "sinister design" to weaken India's international image and called him a "leader of anti-India propaganda", according to reports. The party cited projections by international agencies that rank India among the fastest-growing major economies. BJP president Nitin Nabin said the "disaster" lay in Gandhi's own mind and linked it to the Congress's electoral decline, reports said.

The BJP had criticised Gandhi days earlier over the Bharat Summit in Hyderabad, hosted by the Congress government in Telangana, demanding an apology from him and Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy over remarks by a foreign participant and asking the party to disclose the event's cost, according to reports.

## What the Congress said

Pawan Khera, who heads the Congress's media and publicity department, said: "The government is not bothered about the health of the economy, the government is not bothered about inflation, the government is bothered about Rahul Gandhi speaking about it and the world listening to it." He said the economy was in a bad state and that the government only saw a problem when Gandhi raised it. Congress spokesperson Supriya Shrinate described the BJP's accusations as "boring and stale" in a post on X, reports said.

## Background

Gandhi's speeches abroad have drawn similar BJP attacks before, including over remarks at Cambridge University in 2023 and during a US visit in 2024. The Congress has campaigned on unemployment and prices, while the government points to India's growth rate and its manufacturing incentive schemes.

The Election Commission has previously rejected the Congress's allegations of voter-roll manipulation, and the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in several states has become a central point of dispute between the government and opposition parties.

## What happens next

The row is likely to carry into Parliament's winter session, which reports say is expected to begin in the first week of December; the dates have not yet been formally notified.
